title: Interpolation between product norms
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $q,c\in\mathbb R$ with $q>2$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space. If $\|f\|_{q,P}\le e^c\|f\|_{2,P}$, then $\|f\|_{2,P}\le e^{cq/(q-2)}\|f\|_{1,P}$, where $\|f\|_{r,P}=(\mathbb E_P|f|^r)^{1/r}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q>2$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. If $\|f\|_{q,P}\le e^c\|f\|_{2,P}$, then $\|f\|_{2,P}\le e^{cq/(q-2)}\|f\|_{1,P}$.
